To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic renal failure with progressive deterioration of renal function can develop many years after cessation of cisplatin chemotherapy.
chronic progressive renal failure can develop after cisplatin treatment, even many years after cessation of chemotherapy.

(a) chronic progressive renal failure may occur after cisplatin chemotherapy, even many years after the end of chemotherapy; (b) in our two cases, renal biopsy revealed tubulointerstitial nephritis with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy; (c) the pathogenesis of chronic cisplatin nephropathy is still unclear, but may be related to tubular cell apoptosis and/or necrosis, which may lead to tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis;
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) to describe two cases of progressive renal failure after cisplatintreatment; (2) to discuss possible causes of the observed renal impairment; and (3) to evaluate the potential role of cisplatin in the pathogenesis of the observed renal failure.

the following questions: Is there a difference between the acute and the chronic effects of cisplatin on renal tubular cells? What are the mechanisms underlying cisplatin-induced chronic nephrotoxic side-effects?
the following questions: (i) What is the mechanism of chronic renal failure after cisplatintreatment? and (ii) How can we prevent this side-effect in future?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic renal failure after cisplatintreatment is rare, but may occur.
chronic renal failure is a rare but serious complication of cisplatin treatment.
chronic renal failure is a possible but rare side-effect after cisplatin treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the long-term nephrotoxic effects of cisplatin should not be underestimated and that the risk of chronic renal failure should be taken into account in the risk/benefit analysis of cisplatin chemotherapy.

cisplatin may induce a severe and progressive chronic renal failure, which is not necessarily related to cumulative cisplatin doses, but may occur even years after cessation of cisplatin administration.
the risk of chronic renal failure after cis-platin treatment is underestimated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nephrotoxic potential of cisplatin is not limited to the time of application, and that long-term follow-up is mandatory in patients treated with this agent.
cisplatin-induced chronic renal failure is not necessarily a benign condition and that the patients should be followed up for a long time.
chronic renal failure can be a late complication of cisplatin treatment.
